newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak union says govt wage move against free mkt.
newsitem.headline: Slovak union says govt wage move against free mkt.

text.p: The Slovak Confederation of Trade Unions (KOZ) on Wednesday sharply criticised a government anouncement on the imposition of wage growth restraints, saying the move goes against free market principles.

"This is just another example when the governemnt again did not inform its partner (trade unions) in the social dialogue about prepared economic measures," KOZ spokeswoman Ruzena Wagnerova told Reuters.
"We did not know anything concrete about what the government is planning," she added.
Wagnerova did not say whether KOZ was planning to protest.

On Tuesday, Deputy Finance Minister Peter Stanek announced after a weekly meeting that the government would implement wage regulations to ensure salaries rise in accordance with industrial productivity increases.
The measure is widely seen as one of a series of measures the government is expected to announce in the coming days to help the economy.
In making the announcement, Stanek said the wages had been growing "far faster than labour productivity, and that is not healthy for the economy".
"Especially the measure on wage regulations, even with so little information we have, appears very much against free market principles," Wagnerova said.
The wage regulations, expected to be implemented on August 1, are to be aimed mainly at loss-making companies, where the government saw inappropriately high wages, Stanek said.

The average real wage rose by 8.1 percent to total 8.198 crowns in the first quarter of this year, some 2.9 percentage points faster than labour productivity, the Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said earlier this month.
The average nominal wage for the period rose 14.6 percent, year-on-year.
Fast rising wages without the corresponding increase in productivity has been one of the biggest concerns voiced by analysts over the economy.
